steps.note: S1.3.1.1.1 states the row-by-row subtract/add/restore and that the net target change $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ is independent of the scratch values $a,c$, quoting line 748.
S1.3.1.1.2 gives the bit-case central coefficient $|S\cap T|\bmod 2$, side injection cancelling exactly the intersection-one neighbours, and self coefficient 1.
S1.3.1.1.2 gives the complex central coefficient $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$ with side injection cancelling intersections zero and two, matching the paper.
S1.3.1.1.3 states the inverse schedule $X\gets X-Y$, the stages $(x,y)\to(x,y+x)\to(-y,y+x)\to(-y,x)$, and that each invocation restores its own scratch wires.

The plan gives only the central loss (S1.3.1.3.3), the side edge 2->5 (S1.3.1.3.4) and a general remark that the other edges split along $A=B\perp P$, $F=\langle t\rangle\perp t^\perp$ (S1.3.1.3.5); the per-edge residuals and their dimensions (the table) are never stated.
S1.3.1.3.4 states $\langle t_X\rangle\subset t_Y^\perp$ for neighbours and the residual $P\otimes\langle t_X,t_Y\rangle^\perp$ of dimension $h-2$.
The plan states the only decreasing edge is center 3->4 losing $h$, the telescoping to sinks $Wm-N$ minus sources $N$ giving $Wm-2N$, and the $2L$ correction with $L=Ich$.
S1.3.3.3 only asserts that every nonzero binary residual has an orthonormal basis; the nondegenerate/nonalternating argument and the absorption of alternating planes are not given.
S1.3.1.6 gives $L/N=300c/v$ equal to $100/539$ (bit) and $101/539$ (complex), both below $1/2$.
S1.3.3.1 states the weight identity, additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, and $q_V-q_U=\sum_v\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]$ over an orthonormal residual basis, negated on a decreasing edge.
S1.3.3.2 states odd weight, the phase $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}$ as an affine combination of the character, and $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$ giving $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

The plan says the kernels number $s_{\rm c}$ (S1.3.3, S1.3.3.3) and that the result holds on any number of columns, but never states that on $k$ columns each residual vector contributes one factor $K_{e,v}^{\otimes k}$ acting on all columns.

S1.3.3.4 gives frames $I$ and $C^{\otimes m}$, $C^{-1}$ on the 27 coordinates of $\operatorname{supp}(u_a)$, repair by $Z_{a,k}$ and $i^{27k}Z_{a,k}$ via $C=iZC^{-1}Z$; S1.3.3.5 negates the $X$ outputs.
S1.3.1.6 has $L/N<1/2$, S1.3.2.3 the deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$ from $W_{\rm b}m$, and S1.3.2 $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$.
S1.3.4 states $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$, matching the paper.
S1.3.4 states $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$, matching the paper.
S1.3.4 states both deficits exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, $\log m<20$ gives $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-\eta)$, hence $s/W<m^\tau$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.
S1.4.1.1 states the factorization into invertible lower-triangular factors by repeatedly eliminating around the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row, with $\Pi$ having exactly $a$ ones.

S1.4.1 fixes an odd prime $q$ avoiding the denominators of the factorization and works over $\mathbb Z/q^b$ with invertible lower-triangular factors; it omits the diagonal-numerator condition but carries the defining choice.
S1.4.1.2 states the $O(V)$ cost by updating coordinates in descending physical order while earlier coordinates keep their original values.
S1.4.1.3 gives $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, an interchange, $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$, yielding $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange, $a$ in all.
Only $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$ appears (S1.5.9); $E$, $B$, $\nu$, $C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\}$ and $C_0=128mB^2$ are never defined.
The arithmetic-depth recurrence $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$ with leaf bound $8e$ does not appear; S1.5.9 only asserts the depth bound.
The unrolling $B^{k+1}\le B^2d^\nu$ and the bound $8B^2d^{\nu+1}$ are absent; S1.5.9 asserts depth at most $C_0d^{C_1}$ without derivation.

S1.5.9 states the $p+\Delta$ / $\Delta+3$ bit reservation and $\Delta=o(p)$ from $\epsilon C_1<1$, but not the defining link that depth $\ell$ means values in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ of modulus at most $2^\ell$, so the exactness is asserted rather than derived; marked absent under uncertainty.
S1.5.10 states absolute row sum one, preservation of disk arrays, and final truncation error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

summary: P01 is strong on the bank-exchange network (4/4), the rank-saving constants (4/4), the matrix shear (4/4) and the phase interface except the k-column tensoring (3/4); it misses the residual table and the F2 orthonormal-basis argument in the label budget (3/5), and on the simultaneous layer it gives only the disk/truncation step, asserting the depth bound and register sizing without the constants, recurrence, unrolling or depth-to-size link (1/5). Total 19 of 26 present.
